resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (resale housing inspection)
resale_co.lead_time: No minimum lead time published. The owner must notify Licenses and Inspections within 7 calendar days of a resale (Code 318-6); an expedited inspection within 5 days of the request costs $200.
requirements: Carbon monoxide detector in the hallway outside the bedrooms, within 10 feet of each bedroom (one per hallway on each bedroom floor)
Fire extinguisher 2A 10 BC mounted no higher than 5 feet, within 10 feet of the kitchen
All windows open, close and lock; screens on windows and patio doors without rips
Outlets grounded; GFCI outlets working near water sources
Toilets flush properly, no leaks under sinks
Oven and stove working with an anti-tilt bracket
Overflow pipe on the water heater
Heater certification and chimney certification before the CO is issued
Railings for 4 or more steps or 30 inches and above
House number on the home; exterior maintained
No active, open or unpaid permits

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Housing Inspection Request (listed as Residential CO Application on the Licenses & Inspections page) and return it to Caitlyn Bryant or Anthony Trappanese by email to HousingInspection@twp.burlington.nj.us or fax 609-239-6293. Licenses & Inspections is at 851 Old York Road.

evidence.quote: The owner or occupant of a rooming, multifamily, rental or residential unit may not rent, resell or occupy such unit without a certificate of continued occupancy.
shall notify the Department of Licenses and Inspections within seven calendar days of any resale or rerental of any such unit
Resale inspection fees for a single-family house, townhouse and a condominium unit shall be $100, with a reinspection fee of $50.
Housing/Rental/Apartment Inspections are to provide minimum, reasonable standards before the occupancy of a home/apartment
Certificate of Occupancy is valid for 60 days after date of issuance.
Heater certifications and Chimney certifications are required on all Single Family, Townhouses, and Condo Re-sale and Rental properties, prior to issuance of Certificate of Occupancy.
RETURN FORM TO : Caitlyn Bryant or Anthony Trappanese FAX: 609-239-6293 OR EMAIL: HousingInspection@twp.burlington.nj.us
THIS IS NOT A COMPLETE LIST OF EVERYTHING THAT IS CHECKED DURING AN INSPECTION, BUT THE MOST COMMON ITEMS THAT PREVENT A C.C.O. TO BE ISSUED.
Anthony Trappanese, Housing Inspector/Zoning Officer/Property Maintenance Inspector Office Hours: Monday-Friday 8:00A.M.-4:00P.M. (609)239-5845 atrappanese@twp.burlington.nj.us

resale_co.notes: Required by Township Code Chapter 318 (Housing Standards), Article II: Section 318-6 says a residential unit may not be resold or occupied without a certificate of continued occupancy, and the Department may issue a temporary certificate for up to 30 days for minor repairs that do not affect health and safety. Section 318-8 (amended by Ord. No. 2023-OR-029) sets the same fees as the township fee sheet. The code was read through the ecode360 print view (BU2696 is the Township code; BU2898 in the leads is Burlington City's). If a re-inspection is not done within 60 days of the original inspection, a new inspection and fee are required; this also applies if the CO expires before closing, and heater and chimney certifications expire with the CO. Anthony Trappanese's direct email is atrappanese@twp.burlington.nj.us. The Licenses & Inspections page lists Caitlyn Bryant at (609)239-5846; the department's main line is (609) 239-5847.

fire_cert.notes: The fire code enforcing agency for Burlington Township is the fire district (Burlington Township Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention). The district's own page names Fire Official Matthew Tomaszewski (609-239-5850, mtomaszewski@btfd.org) and says its regular inspections exclude owner-occupied dwellings, while the DCA directory (survey 7/22/2026) still lists Ashley L Johnson (ajohnson@btfd.org) and lists 'Burlington Twp Inspections' at 851 Old York Rd, (609) 239-5847 for smoke detector compliance. The township page says its housing inspector checks smoke detectors, CO detectors and the extinguisher, and Township Code 318-23 applies the smoke alarm rule at resale, so the resale smoke/CO check is done in the township housing inspection with no separate fire district fee found. This is inferred from these sources; no page states it in one sentence. The township page and 2018 items sheet still list the extinguisher although P.L.2025, c.19 (February 3, 2025) removed it from the state rule.
